solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Takes back fruit unopened

indicators.note: something unopened has lost its opening, so the word's front letter goes

parts.note: greengages are small green plums

explanation.surface: A shopper returns a bag of fruit they never even opened.
explanation.walkthrough: GREENGAGES loses its first letter G to leave RE-ENGAGES.
explanation.definitionFit: To re-engage staff is to hire them again, which is taking them back into employment.

clue.text: Fumes on board endanger a vessel

indicators.note: the letters are carried aboard the following words, sitting inside them

parts.note: the last letter of the first word, the second word, and the start of the third run together

explanation.surface: Toxic fumes aboard ship put the whole vessel at risk.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who fumes is angry and rants, and rants furiously, which is a verb sense of raves.

clue.text: How to make Mo and Damon correspond

parts.words: How to make Mo and Damon
parts.note: surface reading: a recipe for getting two people, Mo and Damon, together

parts.words: How to make Mo and Damon
parts.note: setter's reading: the letters of 'Mo and' rearranged spell the name Damon, so swapping letters turns one into the other

explanation.surface: Advice on how to get two pen friends, Mo and Damon, writing to each other.
explanation.walkthrough: M-O-A-N-D and D-A-M-O-N use the same five letters, so the wordplay is literal letter-swapping.
explanation.definitionFit: To correspond is to write to one another, trading mail back and forth over time.

clue.text: Large number turn to rum and ale unfortunately

indicators.note: things going unfortunately have gone wrong, so the letters before it are thrown out of order

parts.note: your go is your turn in a game
rum in the old British sense of strange or peculiar
the three letters of the beer, rearranged

explanation.surface: A huge crowd turns to drinking rum and ale, with bad results.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rum' looks like a drink beside 'ale', but here it is the adjective meaning odd.
explanation.definitionFit: A good deal means a lot, a considerable quantity, so it can stand in for a large number.

clue.text: Carriage crowd in conversation

indicators.note: in conversation means spoken, so we want a word that sounds like the clue's synonym

parts.note: the gate is the number of spectators at a sports match

explanation.surface: A carriage of people chatting as they travel together.
explanation.definitionFit: Carriage can mean the way a person holds and moves the body, which is their manner of walking.

clue.text: Cabinet has covert broadcast cut short

indicators.note: cutting something short trims its tail, so the final letter is dropped

parts.note: covert means hidden or secret
a programme that has been broadcast has been aired

explanation.surface: A government cabinet's covert briefing gets cut off mid-broadcast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cabinet' suggests ministers, but it is the piece of furniture.
explanation.definitionFit: A secretaire is a writing desk with drawers and a fold-down top, a type of furniture cabinet.

clue.text: Remains of old underwear

definitions.meaning: first meaning: is left behind, does not leave
second meaning: a historical corset stiffened with bone

explanation.surface: Archaeologists dig up the last scraps of some ancient underclothes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Remains' reads as a noun for relics, but it is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a verb for continuing to be present and a plural noun for a laced, boned bodice once worn by women.

clue.text: I'm sorry about fatuous, hollow pranks

indicators.note: about suggests turning round, so the apology is read backwards

parts.note: the exclamation of apology after a slip

indicators.note: a hollow word has had its insides scooped out, leaving only the end letters

parts.note: the first and last letters of the word

explanation.surface: Someone apologises for their silly, empty practical jokes.
explanation.definitionFit: Spoofs are hoaxes or comic tricks played on someone, much the same as pranks.

clue.text: Pollock, perhaps digest rope securing a boat

parts.note: a digest or summary of a paper is an abstract
a painter is the line at a small boat's bow used to tie it up

explanation.surface: A pollock, the fish, digests a mooring rope tied to a boat.
explanation.walkthrough: Pollock looks like the fish, which suits the boat and rope; it is Jackson Pollock, the American drip painter.
explanation.definitionFit: Jackson Pollock was a leading figure of non-representational art, an example of this kind of artist.

clue.text: Hose attachment's main sales feature in poster

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other

parts.note: one who posts a letter sends it
USP is a unique selling point, the main thing a product is marketed on

explanation.surface: A garden hose's key selling point is shown on an advertising poster.
explanation.walkthrough: Hose here means stockings, not a garden pipe; the 's stands for 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: A suspender is the clip and strap that holds up stockings, which are also called hose.

clue.text: How you write this answer in wins medals

indicators.note: in tells us to put one piece inside the other

parts.note: wins are victories
this is an across clue, so the answer is written left to right across the grid

explanation.surface: A self-referential instruction about writing the answer among a list of victories and medals.
explanation.walkthrough: The direction of an entry in the grid is part of the wordplay: this clue sits in the across list, which supplies the inserted word.
explanation.definitionFit: The Victoria Cross is Britain's highest award for gallantry, so its plural names a set of military decorations.

clue.text: Drink in small local

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for small
handy means conveniently near by

explanation.surface: Having a drink in a small neighbourhood pub.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain the local is your nearby pub, which makes the surface convincing; here it means nearby. A shandy is beer mixed with lemonade.
explanation.definitionFit: A shandy is a beverage of beer diluted with lemonade or ginger beer, so it is a kind of drink.

clue.text: Inevitably do without mass and church

indicators.note: without means lacking, so a letter is removed

parts.note: to do a task is to perform it
M is the physics symbol for mass
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: Someone inevitably ends up skipping Mass and church services.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mass' looks like the church service beside 'church', but it is the physics letter M.
explanation.definitionFit: Perforce is an old-fashioned adverb meaning by necessity, unavoidably.

clue.text: Disco genre newly appreciated

indicators.note: newly suggests the letters are made over into a fresh form

parts.note: the ten letters of these two words

explanation.surface: Disco as a style of music finally gets the respect it deserves.
explanation.definitionFit: Work that is recognised is acknowledged and valued by others, as when merit is formally appreciated.

clue.text: Drag grand star back to an unoccupied carriage

parts.note: to lug is to haul something heavy
G is short for grand, a thousand

indicators.note: back says read the star's name the other way round

parts.note: Vega is a bright star in the constellation Lyra
taken as written

explanation.surface: A grand star is dragged back to an empty railway carriage.
explanation.walkthrough: Railway luggage vans carry bags, not passengers, which is why the carriage is called unoccupied.
explanation.definitionFit: A luggage van is a railway wagon for baggage, with no seats for passengers travelling.

clue.text: Record about a reindeer, one barely performs

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so one piece goes round another

parts.note: an LP is a long-playing record
taken as written
Dancer is one of Santa's reindeer

explanation.surface: A Christmas record about a reindeer whose performance is barely passable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Barely' reads as 'hardly', but means nearly naked.
explanation.definitionFit: A lap dancer is an erotic entertainer who performs close to a customer while scantily clothed.

clue.text: Police unit following a tart

indicators.note: following means coming after, so the unit named before it is placed second

parts.note: taken as written
CID is the Criminal Investigation Department of a British police force

explanation.surface: Police officers trail a woman of loose morals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Following' puts the police unit after the A. 'Tart' tempts as a pastry or a woman, but it is the adjective for sour.
explanation.definitionFit: Something tart has a sharp sour taste, which is a quality of an acid.

clue.text: Frantic swimmers lapping incessantly

indicators.note: lapping means wrapping round, so one piece encloses the other

parts.note: fish are creatures that swim
ever means always, without stopping

explanation.surface: Frantic swimmers keep doing lengths of the pool non-stop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lapping' suggests swimming lengths, but it signals wrapping around.
explanation.definitionFit: Feverish activity is wild and hurried, done in a state of nervous excitement.

clue.text: I popped into friend's for a beer

indicators.note: popped into suggests slipping in to take another letter's place

parts.note: taken as written
a pal is a friend, with the 's as S

explanation.surface: I dropped round to a friend's house for a beer.
explanation.walkthrough: The I goes in where the A of PALS was.
explanation.definitionFit: Pils is a short form of pilsner, a pale lager originally brewed in Bohemia.

clue.text: He attends an opening ceremony, with one who retains the gold

parts.note: a do is a party or function
or is gold in heraldry
one who keeps something is a keeper

explanation.surface: A dignitary attends an opening ceremony with a guardian of the gold.
explanation.walkthrough: The opening is a doorway, not an event being formally opened.
explanation.definitionFit: A doorkeeper is a porter who guards an entrance and lets visitors in.

clue.text: Makes changes to what happens at noon

definitions.meaning: second meaning, read cryptically: at midday the morning, a.m., comes to an end

explanation.surface: Someone revises their routine for what goes on at lunchtime.
explanation.walkthrough: Split the answer as AM ENDS for the second reading.
explanation.definitionFit: To amend a text or law is to alter or improve it, so amends means makes changes.

clue.text: A US city concealing an Athenian element

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: concealing means hiding inside, so one piece holds the other

parts.note: NY is New York
Timon of Athens is Shakespeare's misanthrope

explanation.surface: An American city hides an element from ancient Athens.
explanation.definitionFit: Antimony is a brittle silvery metalloid, chemical symbol Sb, number 51 in the periodic table.

clue.text: Fight to block the French tariffs

indicators.note: to block is to sit inside and stop the way, so one piece goes within another

parts.note: les is French for the, in the plural
to vie is to compete or contend

explanation.surface: Battling to stop France imposing trade tariffs.
explanation.definitionFit: Levies are charges or taxes imposed by authority, as tariffs are duties on imports.

clue.text: Hide from kids influenced to be outspoken

indicators.note: outspoken here means spoken out loud, so we want a sound-alike

parts.note: someone influenced has been swayed

explanation.surface: Children are persuaded to speak their minds frankly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hide from kids' sounds like concealing things from children; it is leather from young goats.
explanation.definitionFit: Suede is leather with a napped finish, traditionally made from the skin of young goats.

clue.text: Cries to axe top Members of Parliament

indicators.note: axing the top cuts off the head, so the first letter goes in this down answer

parts.note: howls are loud cries

explanation.surface: There are calls to sack senior MPs.
explanation.walkthrough: A parliament is the collective noun for a group of owls.
explanation.definitionFit: A gathering of these birds is called a parliament, so each bird is a member of one.

clue.text: Totally innocent, listen as each law is broken

indicators.note: something broken is smashed apart, so its letters are put back in another order

parts.note: the fifteen letters of these four words

explanation.surface: A defendant claims total innocence, telling the court to hear how every law was broken.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes someone with no guilt or stain at all, entirely blameless.

clue.text: Afterthought added to artist's files

parts.note: RA is a Royal Academician, with the 's as S
PS is a postscript added to a letter

explanation.surface: An artist's archive gets a last-minute note appended.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Files' looks like folders of papers; it is the tools.
explanation.definitionFit: Rasps are coarse metal tools used for shaping wood, much like files.

clue.text: Detectives indict or acquit

parts.note: DIs are detective inspectors
to indict is to charge formally with a crime

explanation.surface: Detectives must decide whether to bring charges against a suspect or let them go.
explanation.definitionFit: A court that discharges a defendant releases them, which is close to clearing them of blame.
